problem: Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(3,1)$ where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$, given that $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖=2,$ and the unit tangent vector to the curve is $\,T(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$
worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(\frac{\pi }{2})=⟨3,1⟩,$ since the point $P(3,1)$ is at the tip of $r(\frac{\pi }{2}).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t)$, ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩=⟨-1,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}=\frac{2}{1}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}=⟨-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{\pi }{2})+R(\frac{\pi }{2})N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨3,1⟩+2⟨-1,0⟩=⟨1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
